status: REGRESSION confirmed by the scorer of record (grasp 0.04). H10 FAIL: the critic repair did not restore action sensitivity. Closes the actor-critic line; see g1_piston_run9_result.json.
what_ran: Run 7's residual arm plus NUM_Q=10, TARGET_SUBSET=2, ACTOR_Q_AGG=mean, N_STEP=3 (run8_preregistration.json). Durable storage. 63,780 env steps, 450 updates (150 actor) before the stop.

readout.note_on_scale: in-trainer baseline for the unchanged policy is 0.76; 0.92 during warmup is the zero residual (BC). Collapse begins with the first actor updates, exactly as in runs 6 and 7.
readout.critic: loss 27.9 at update 75 (3-step targets) -> 0.85 by update 450: the ensemble fit its targets. Q rose to 3.42.
readout.entropy: alpha 0.0501 -> 0.0467, logp 1.92 -> 1.91 at target 1.913: regulating correctly.

reading: Three arms now collapse identically once the actor updates: direct head (run 6), bounded residual (run 7), bounded residual with a repaired critic (run 8). The entropy term is verified fixed in all three. The common factor is that the actor follows a critic gradient that does not encode which action directions break the grasp. A larger ensemble and longer-horizon targets change the critic's VALUE estimates (Q 3.4 vs 0.6) without changing its ACTION sensitivity, which is a property of the data: demonstration actions lie within 0.4 deg of the policy's own, and 180-dimensional exploration noise at ~8 transitions per dimension does not localise which dimension mattered.
pending: H10 probe on run 8's final critic (queued after scoring) will state the sensitivity number directly; scorer-of-record grasp for runs 7 and 8; reversed-order BC probe.
what_this_settles: Under this compute budget (~1.5 s per update, ~600 updates per run, one 16 GB GPU), off-policy actor-critic fine-tuning of this chunked VLA policy does not preserve a working behaviour, and the reason is measured at every layer: entropy geometry (fixed), then critic action-insensitivity (not fixed by ensemble size or n-step).
options_recorded_for_the_decision: A: contrastive negatives -- construct transitions whose actions are the BC chunk perturbed along ONE dimension at a time and whose rewards come from the simulator, so the critic can attribute failure to a direction. Costly: each negative is a simulator rollout (~150 s per condition).
B: shrink the RL action space to a handful of task-relevant dimensions and 1-2 DCT components, so ~8 transitions per dimension becomes hundreds.
C: write up the measured anatomy with the BC result as the deliverable; no further RL runs.
D: produce a pressing demonstration by extending the data (scripted or teleoperated press) and cloning it; not RL, but yields the functional video.

H10_probe_final_critic.verdict: FAIL. frac(Q_bc > Q_perturbed) = 0.49 / 0.47 (chance), Q gap to its own drifted chunk 1.4% / 0.8%, drifted chunk rated higher on 96-100% of frames. A 10-critic RLPD-aggregated ensemble with 3-step targets is exactly as action-insensitive as the 2-head critic. The registered falsifier holds: ensemble and n-step are not sufficient; the remedy was to remove the critic (run 9).
